messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Regarding warning related to distance interval
parts:
Yash

Thanks for clarifying that you are using Distance for Windows.

Let me explain the message you have received.  This is the situation that led to the message:  you collected data on animals that occur in groups, you measured exact distances to the centre of each group, you chose to fit detection functions to the distance data by using binned data rather than exact distances, finally you requested that size bias adjustment be carried out in the mean group size adjustment using regression.

This set of circumstances generated a warning (not an error) from the software.  A warning is issued when you instruct the software to do two things that are inconsistent.  The inconsistency here is using binned distances for detection function fitting while using exact distances in the size bias regression analysis.  The software is simply advising you of how the software is conducting the analysis.  It is not indicating an error.

I do not understand your comment about "results differ when changing the interval but not the distance interval".

Respected sir,
I am using Distance software 7.3 (not R -distance). as per your reply i changed distance interval manually in  input properties. after adjustment of interval i got warning in Log message such as “** Warning: Exact distance values, rather than distance intervals, have been used in size bias regression calculations. **”. Results also differs if I change the interval and without change in distance interval. this message is showing some error or it is formality please give me some suggestion.
